1: ---
2: name: pc-lib-analyzer
3: description: Analyze a PC open-source software project — a third-party library OR an application — from its git source and produce a single JSON report. Give it a git URL (or a local checkout path) of a Python / C/C++ / Java / JS-TS project. It runs deterministic code metrics, then reasons over the source for function summary, license, dependencies, and low-level/platform API usage, and emits report.json conforming to references/report_schema.json. Designed to be invoked end-to-end (e.g. from an external script or UI via `claude --agent pc-lib-analyzer`).
4: tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
5: ---
6: 
7: You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
8: application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
9: analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
10: script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
11: First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
12: service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
13: native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
14: existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
15: → `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
16: This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).
17: 
18: ## Input
19: A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
20: the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.
21: 
22: ## Procedure
23: 
24: 1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
25:    (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
26:    ```bash
27:    git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
28:    ```
29:    Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
30:    local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.
31: 
32:    **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
33:    `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
34:    把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
35:    用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
36:    BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。
37: 
38: 2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
39:    its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
40:    (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
41:    Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
42:    will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
43:    `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
44:    ```bash
45:    python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
46:    ```
47: 
48: 2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
49:    **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
50:    the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
51:    NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
52:    e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
53:    ```bash
54:    codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
55:    codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
56:    codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
57:    ```
58:    Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1 and 7. If a codegraph call fails
59:    (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
60:    note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
61:    If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
62:    time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).
63: 
64: 3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
65:    file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
66:    - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
67:    - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
68:    - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
69:    - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
70:      (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
71:    - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
72:      (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
73:    - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
74:      (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
75:      exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
76:    - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
77:      (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
78:      BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
79:      runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
80: 
81:    **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
82:    **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
83:    内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
84:    dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
85:    dim8→`runtime_surface.json` 与 `build_env.json`、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
86:    dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
87:    **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
88:    你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
89:    综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。
90: 
91:    Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
92:    representative source files. Cross-check the
93:    script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
94:    `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.
95: 
96:    **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
97:    上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
98:    正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
99:    `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
100:    代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
101:    curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
102:    由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
103:    仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。
104: 
105:    **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
106:    - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
107:      `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
108:    - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
109:      `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
110:      目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
111:      `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
112:    - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
113:      `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
114:      生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
115:      `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
116:    - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
117:      如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
118:      （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。
119: 
120: 3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
121:    are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
122:    OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
123:    skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
124:    ```bash
125:    node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
126:    ```
127:    It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
128:    and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
129:    lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
130:    `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
131:    but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)
132: 
133: 3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
134:    above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
135:    `harmony_adaptation` (feasibility / difficulty / path / blockers / effort +
136:    the `porting_class` closed axis — no_adaptation / recompile_only /
137:    needs_adaptation_full（全部可适配）/ needs_adaptation_partial（部分可适配）/ infeasible —
138:    of porting to HarmonyOS NEXT PC) plus, when some functionality is truly unportable,
139:    the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
140:    category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
141:    **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
142:    `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
143:    `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
144:    difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
145:    场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
146:    drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
147:    第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and **reuse their `evidence`**.
148:    Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref
149:    the capability_profile scenario OR cloud_services via `source_capability`). 若
150:    `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
151:    某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
152:    `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
153:    this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
154:    production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
155:    seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
156:    评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
157:    **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
158:    project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
159:    internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
160:    their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
161:    `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
162:    **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
163:    unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
164:    `unadaptable_apis`.
165: 
166: 3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
167:    re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
168:    and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
169:    平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
170:    - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
171:      出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
172:    - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
173:      `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
174:    - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或
175:      `runtime_surface.network` 出现厂商云域名（amazonaws.com/firebaseio.com/sentry.io…）→ `cloud_services`
176:      应 present 且推出对应 vendor；`cloud_services.present` 时 dim-9 应有 INTERNET 权限项。
177:    - `required_permissions[].source_capability` 必须指向一个 present 场景，或字面量 `"cloud_services"`（当权限源自云服务时）。
178:    补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
179:    `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**
180: 
181: 4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
182:    `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
183:    `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
184:    `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
185:    ```bash
186:    python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
187:    ```
188:    它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
189:    `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
190:    fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，最后**原子写**
191:    `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
192:    对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。
193: 
194:    **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
195:    `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
196:    (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
197:    `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
198:    `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
199:    may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
200:    this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
201:    某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
202:    `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。
203:    子目录依赖的兄弟内部模块（如 chromium 的 `//base`、`//net`，经 BUILD.gn 引入、非外部包）记入
204:    `dependencies[]` 并标 `locality:local`（内部 monorepo 模块），不当作外部依赖。When the package name ≠
205:    import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`
206:    (其它已知名/旧名/CMake find_package 名/Maven groupId:artifactId) and
207:    `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
208:    can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
209:    最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +
210:    `registry_name` when its `name` isn't the canonical package name. Set `library.bindings` —
211:    the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
212:    (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).
213: 
214:    In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
215:    (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
216:    and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
217:    (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
218:    include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
219:    (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
220:    their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
221:    Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
222:    Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
223:    `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
224:    platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
225:    Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
226:    (`feasibility`/`porting_class`/`effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`)
227:    must use schema enum values (`effort.level` is server-derived — don't fill it);
228:    `recommended_path`/`blockers[].category`/`harmony_status` are open
229:    vocab; each blocker carries its `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.
230: 
231:    For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
232:    concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
233:    (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
234:    `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
235:    本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
236:    (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
237:    parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.
238: 
239:    The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
240:    the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
241:    you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
242:    `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
243:    into the skills.
244: 
245: 5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
246:    absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
247:    language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
248:    runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.
249: 
250: ## Rules
251: - The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
252:   target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
253:   proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
254: - All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
255:   the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
256:   path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
257:   which aborts the analysis with no report.
258: - Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
259:   `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
260: - Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
261:   re-counting.
262: - If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
263:   API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
264: - One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
265:   Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
266: - **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
267:   `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
268:   and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
269:   breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
270:   fanning out into research agents.
271: - **解释性维度只能由你推理产出，绝不自写脚本去提取/解析/序列化它们。** dim 1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11
272:   的每个 `blocks/<name>.json` **必须由你用 `Write` 工具直接写出**，内容来自你自己的阅读与判断。
273:   **本流程唯一被授权运行的脚本只有三个**：`.claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py`
274:   （dim 2–4 计数）、`scripts/harmony_adapted.js`（dim 6 鸿蒙盖章）、`scripts/assemble_report.py`
275:   （组装）。除此之外**禁止写任何 Python/shell 脚本**——不许写正则去扫 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/
276:   `package.json` 抽依赖，不许拿脚本当 JSON dump/打分/reshape 工具，尤其不要 `extract_*.py` /
277:   `build_*.py` / `stamp_*.py` / `split_*.py` 这类自造中间件。想快速摸底只能用**只读**的
278:   `Grep`/`Glob`/`codegraph`（context/query/callers）探查，**但结论与 JSON 一律由你判断产出**——
279:   这些维度的准确性正来自模型判断，正则会把别名/接口名（如 `find_package(PNG)`）/条件编译/
280:   示例目录判错。（唯一例外见 3a：`harmony_adapted.js` 是被授权的事实盖章脚本。）

You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
→ `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).

## Input
A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.

## Procedure

1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
   (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
   ```
   Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
   local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.

   **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
   `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
   把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
   用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
   BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。

2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
   its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
   (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
   Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
   will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
   `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
   ```

2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
   **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
   the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
   NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
   e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
   ```bash
   codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
   codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
   codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
   ```
   Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1 and 7. If a codegraph call fails
   (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
   note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
   If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
   time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).

3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
   file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
   - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
   - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
     (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
   - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
     (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
     exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
   - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
     BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
     runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)

   **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
   **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
   内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
   dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
   dim8→`runtime_surface.json` 与 `build_env.json`、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
   dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
   **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
   你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
   综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。

   Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
   representative source files. Cross-check the
   script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
   `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.

   **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
   上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
   正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
   `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
   代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
   curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
   由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
   仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。

   **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
   - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
     `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
   - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
     `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
     目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
     `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
   - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
     `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
     生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
     `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
   - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
     如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
     （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。

3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
   are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
   OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
   skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
   ```bash
   node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
   ```
   It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
   and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
   lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
   `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
   but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)

3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
   above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
   `harmony_adaptation` (feasibility / difficulty / path / blockers / effort +
   the `porting_class` closed axis — no_adaptation / recompile_only /
   needs_adaptation_full（全部可适配）/ needs_adaptation_partial（部分可适配）/ infeasible —
   of porting to HarmonyOS NEXT PC) plus, when some functionality is truly unportable,
   the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
   category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
   **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
   `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
   `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
   difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
   场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
   drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
   第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and **reuse their `evidence`**.
   Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref
   the capability_profile scenario OR cloud_services via `source_capability`). 若
   `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
   某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
   `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
   this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
   production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
   seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
   评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
   **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
   project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
   internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
   their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
   `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
   **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
   unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
   `unadaptable_apis`.

3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
   re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
   and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
   平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
   - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
     出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
   - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
     `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
   - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或

     应 present 且推出对应 vendor；`cloud_services.present` 时 dim-9 应有 INTERNET 权限项。
   - `required_permissions[].source_capability` 必须指向一个 present 场景，或字面量 `"cloud_services"`（当权限源自云服务时）。
   补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
   `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**

4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
   `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
   `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
   `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
   ```
   它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
   `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
   fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，最后**原子写**
   `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
   对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。

   **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
   `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
   (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
   `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
   `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
   may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
   this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
   某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
   `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。

   import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`

   `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
   can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
   最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +

   the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
   (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).

   In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
   (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
   and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
   (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
   include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
   (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
   their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
   Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
   Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
   `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
   platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
   Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
   (`feasibility`/`porting_class`/`effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`)
   must use schema enum values (`effort.level` is server-derived — don't fill it);
   `recommended_path`/`blockers[].category`/`harmony_status` are open
   vocab; each blocker carries its `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.

   For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
   concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
   (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
   `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
   本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
   (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
   parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.

   The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
   the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
   you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
   `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
   into the skills.

5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
   absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
   language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
   runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.

  the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
  path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
  which aborts the analysis with no report.
- Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
  `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
- Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
  re-counting.
- If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native

1: Building and Installing
2: -----------------------
3: 
4: See the "INSTALL" file.
5: 
6: 
7: Initiator and Responder
8: -----------------------
9: 
10: libmtp implements an MTP initiator, which means it initiate
11: MTP sessions with devices. The devices responding are known
12: as MTP responders. libmtp runs on something with a USB host
13: controller interface, using libusb to access the host
14: controller.
15: 
16: If you're more interested in the MTP responders, gadgets like
17: MP3 players, mobile phones etc, look into:
18: - MeeGo:s Buteo Sync:
19:   https://github.com/nemomobile/buteo-mtp
20:   https://wiki.merproject.org/wiki/Buteo/MTP
21: - Android has an MTP responder implementation:
22:   https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/media/jni/
23: - Ubuntu/Ricardo Salveti has mtp-server and libmtp-server going:
24:   https://code.launchpad.net/~phablet-team/mtp/trunk
25:   https://bazaar.launchpad.net/~phablet-team/mtp/trunk/files
26: 
27: Heritage
28: --------
29: 
30: libmtp is based on several ancestors:
31: 
32: * libptp2 by Mariusz Woloszyn was the starting point used
33:   by Richard A. Low for the initial starter port. You can
34:   find it at https://libptp.sourceforge.net/
35: 
36: * libgphoto2 by Mariusz Woloszyn and Marcus Meissner was
37:   used at a later stage since it was (is) more actively
38:   maintained. libmtp tracks the PTP implementation in
39:   libgphoto2 and considers it an upstream project. We will
40:   try to submit anything generally useful back to libgphoto2
41:   and not make double efforts. In practice this means we
42:   use ptp.c, ptp.h and ptp-pack.c verbatim from the libgphoto2
43:   source code. If you need to change things in these files,
44:   make sure it is so general that libgphoto2 will want to
45:   merge it to their codebase too. You find libgphoto2 as part
46:   of gPhoto: https://gphoto.sourceforge.net/
47: 
48: * libnjb was a project that Richard and Linus were working
49:   on before libmtp. When Linus took Richards initial port
50:   and made an generic C API he re-used the philosophy and
51:   much code from libnjb. Many of the sample programs are for
52:   example taken quite literally from libnjb. You find it here:
53:   https://libnjb.sourceforge.net/
54: 
55: 
56: Contacting and Contributing
57: ---------------------------
58: 
59: See the project page at https://libmtp.sourceforge.net/
60: We always need your help. There is a mailinglist and a
61: bug report system there.
62: 
63: You can also file github issues at https://github.com/libmtp/libmtp
64: 
65: People who want to discuss MTP devices in fora seem to
66: hang out on the forums at AnythingbutiPod:
67: https://www.anythingbutipod.com/forum/
68: 
69: 
70: Compiling programs for libmtp
71: -----------------------------
72: 
73: libmtp has support for the pkg-config script by adding a libmtp.pc
74: entry in $(prefix)/lib/pkgconfig. To compile a libmtp program,
75: "just" write:
76: 
77: gcc -o foo `pkg-config --cflags --libs libmtp` foo.c
78: 
79: This also simplifies compilation using autoconf and pkg-config: just
80: write e.g.
81: 
82: PKG_CHECK_MODULES(MTP, libmtp)
83: AC_SUBST(MTP_CFLAGS)
84: AC_SUBST(MTP_LIBS)
85: 
86: To have libmtp LIBS and CFLAGS defined. Needless to say, this will
87: only work if you have pkgconfig installed on your system, but most
88: people have nowadays.
89: 
90: If your library is installed in e.g. /usr/local you may have to tell
91: this to pkgconfig by setting the PKG_CONFIG_PATH thus:
92: 
93: export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
94: 
95: 
96: Documentation
97: -------------
98: 
99: Read the API documentation that can be generated with doxygen.
100: It will be output in doc/html if you have Doxygen properly
101: installed. (It will not be created unless you have Doxygen!)
102: 
103: For information about the Media Transfer Protocol, see:
104: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_Transfer_Protocol
105: 
106: The official 1.0 specification for MTP was released by the
107: USB Implementers Forum in may, 2008. Prior to this, only a
108: proprietary Microsoft version was available, and quite a few
109: devices out there still use some aspects of the Microsoft
110: version, which deviates from the specified standard. You can
111: find the official specification here:
112: https://www.usb.org/developers/devclass_docs/MTP_1.0.zip
113: 
114: 
115: The Examples
116: ------------
117: 
118: In the subdirectory "examples" you find a number of
119: command-line tools, illustrating the use of libmtp in very
120: simple terms.
121: 
122: Please do not complain about the usability or documentation
123: of these examples, they look like they do for two reasons:
124: 
125: 1. They are examples, not tools. If they were intended for
126:    day-to-day usage by commandline freaks, I would have
127:    called them "tools" not "examples".
128: 
129: 2. The MTP usage paradigm is that a daemon should hook
130:    the device upon connection, and that it should be
131:    released by unplugging. GUI tools utilizing HAL (hald)
132:    and D-Bus do this much better than any commandline
133:    program ever can. (See below on bugs.) Specificationwise
134:    this is a bug, however it is present in many, many
135:    devices.
136: 
137: That said, if you want to pick up and maintain the examples,
138: please volunteer.
139: 
140: 
141: FAQ: Common Problems
142: --------------------
143: 
144: Some MTP devices have strange pecularities. We try to work around
145: these whenever we can, sometimes we cannot work around it or we
146: cannot test your solution.
147: 
148: * Android locked screen: some devices just report zero files
149:   and no storages when the device screen is locked, it looks like
150:   so:
151: 
152:   mtp-detect
153:   Device 0 (VID=04e8 and PID=6860) is a Samsung Galaxy models (MTP).
154:   Attempting to connect device(s)
155:   Error 1: Get Storage information failed.
156:   Device: SHV-E210K
157:   LIBMTP_Get_Storage(): No data available
158:   OK.
159: 
160:   This is probably so as not to allow the MTP access to be used
161:   as a "backdoor" into the device. Unlock the device before listing
162:   files, set the autolock to some large value or disabled if it
163:   disturbs you, you are causing this to yourself, or should we say
164:   that your vendor is prioritizing security and privacy over
165:   ease-of-use. (You may talk to your vendor about this.)
166: 
167: * mtp-* tools doesn't work because someone else is already hogging
168:   the device
169: 
170:   This is a common problem, the most common case could be that
171:   gphoto2 (which can also talk PTP/MTP) is taking over the device
172:   as soon as it's plugged in. Some distributions are configured that
173:   way. Counter it like this:
174: 
175:   gvfs-mount -s gphoto2
176: 
177:   Then re-attach the device.
178: 
179:   Sometimes some gvfs daemons are running on the
180:   system and hogging the device, try stopping them
181:   with something like these commands:
182: 
183:   killall gvfs-mtp-volume-monitor
184:   killall gvfs-gphoto2-volume-monitor
185: 
186:   Then plug in the device and issue "mtp-detect" to figure out if
187:   this may be the case.
188: 
189: * Generic MTP/PTP disconnect misbehaviour: we have noticed that
190:   Windows Media Player apparently never close the session to an MTP
191:   device. There is a daemon in Windows that "hooks" the device
192:   by opening a PTP session to any MTP device, whenever it is
193:   plugged in. This daemon proxies any subsequent transactions
194:   to/from the device and will never close the session, thus
195:   Windows simply does not close sessions at all.
196: 
197:   For example this means that a device may work the first time
198:   you run some command-line example like "mtp-detect" while
199:   subsequent runs fail.
200: 
201:   Typical sign of this illness: broken pipes on closing sessions,
202:   on the main transfer pipes(s) or the interrupt pipe:
203: 
204:     Closing session
205:     usb_clear_halt() on INTERRUPT endpoint: Broken pipe
206:     OK.
207: 
208:   This means that device manufacturers doesn't notice any problems
209:   with devices that do not correctly handle closing PTP/MTP
210:   sessions, since Windows never do it. The proper way of closing
211:   a session in Windows is to unplug the device, simply put.
212: 
213:   Since libmtp actually tries to close sessions, some devices
214:   may fail since the close session functionality has never been
215:   properly tested, and "it works with Windows" is sort of the
216:   testing criteria at some companies.
217: 
218:   You can get Windows-like behaviour on Linux by running a udev-aware
219:   libmtp GUI client like Rhythmbox or Gnomad2, which will "hook"
220:   the device when you plug it in, and "release" it if you unplug
221:   it, and you start/end you transfer sessions by plugging/unplugging
222:   the USB cable.
223: 
224:   The "Unix way" of running small programs that open the device,
225:   do something, then close the device, isn't really working with
226:   such devices and you cannot expect to have command line tools
227:   like the mtp examples work with them. You could implement new
228:   example programs that just call to a mediating daemon like the
229:   Windows MTP stack does. (And change all programs using libmtp
230:   directly today.)
231: 
232:   If this bug in your device annoys you, contact your device
233:   manufacturer and ask them to test their product with some libmtp
234:   program.
235: 
236: * Samsung Android 2.3.x devices: these have a special MTP stack
237:   with some specific bugs that we have maybe nailed down now.
238:   It suffers from an "immediate connect" syndrome, i.e. you have
239:   to connect to the device within 7 seconds of plugging in, or it
240:   will go numb. This also goes for command-line activity with
241:   the example programs, so this device is better used with a
242:   GUI tool like Rhythmbox, gnomad2...
243: 
244: * Generic USB misbehaviour: some devices behave badly under MTP
245:   and USB mass storage alike, even down to the lowest layers
246:   of USB. You can always discuss such issues at the linux-usb
247:   mailing list if you're using Linux:
248:   https://www.linux-usb.org/mailing.html
249: 
250:   If you have a problem specific to USB mass storage mode, there
251:   is a list of strange behaving devices in the Linux kernel:
252:   https://lxr.linux.no/linux/drivers/usb/storage/unusual_devs.h
253:   You can discuss this too on the mentioned list, for understanding
254:   the quirks, see:
255:   https://www2.one-eyed-alien.net/~mdharm/linux-usb/target_offenses.txt
256: 
257: * Generic certificate misbehaviour. All devices are actually
258:   required to support a device certificate to be able to
259:   encrypt Windows Media (WMA/WMV) files. However there are
260:   obviously a lot of devices out there which doesn't support
261:   this at all but instead crash. Typical printout:
262: 
263:   Error 2: PTP Layer error 02ff: get_device_unicode_property(): failed
264:   to get unicode property.
265: 
266:   This should only affect "mtp-detect", there is no other
267:   application currently retrieveing the certificate (not that we
268:   know anyway).
269: 
270: * Kernel bug on Linux. Linux 2.6.16 is generally speaking required
271:   to use any MTP device under USB 2.0. This is because the EHCI
272:   driver previously did not support zero-length writes to endpoints.
273:   It should work in most cases however, or if you connect it
274:   to an UHCI/OHCI port instead (yielding lower speed). But
275:   please just use a recent kernel.
276: 
277: * Zen models AVI file seeking problem: the Zens cannot parse the
278:   files for the runlength metadata. Do not transfer file with e.g.
279:   mtp-sendfile, use mtp-sendtr and set the length of the track to
280:   the appropriate number of seconds and it will work. In graphical
281:   clients, use a "track transfer" function to send these AVI files,
282:   the Zens need the metadata associated with tracks to play back
283:   movies properly. Movies are considered "tracks" in the MTP world.
284: 
285: * Some devices that disregard the metadata sent with the MTP
286:   commands will parse the files for e.g. ID3 metadata. Some still
287:   of these devices expect only ID3v2.3 metadata and will fail with
288:   a modern ID3v2,4 tag writer, like many of those found in Linux
289:   applications. Windows Media Player use ID3v2.3 only, so many
290:   manufacturers only test this version.
291: 
292: * The Zen Vision:M (possibly more Creative Zens) has a firmware bug
293:   that makes it drop the last two characters off a playlist name.
294:   It is fixed in later firmware.
295: 
296: * For Creative Technology devices, there are hard limits on how
297:   many files can be put onto the device. For a 30 GiB device (like
298:   the Zen Xtra) the limit is 6000, for a 60 GiB device the limit
299:   is 15000 files. For further Creative pecularities, see the
300:   FAQ sections at www.nomadness.net.
301: 
302: * Sandisk sansa c150 and probably several other Sandisk devices
303:   (and possibly devices from other manufacturers) have a dual
304:   mode with MTP and USB mass storage. The device will initially
305:   claim to be mass storage so udev will capture is and make the
306:   use of MTP mode impossible. One way of avoiding it could be to
307:   be to blacklist the "usb-storage" module in
308:   /etc/modprobe.c/blacklist with a row like this:
309:   "blacklist usb-storage". Some have even removed the
310:   "usb-storage.ko" (kernel module file) to avoid loading.
311: 
312: * Sandisk Sansa Fuze has three modes: auto, MTP or mass storage
313:   (MSC). Please set it to MTP to avoid problems with libmtp.
314: 
315: * The iriver devices (possibly all of them) cannot handle the
316:   enhanced GetObjectPropList MTP command (0x9805) properly. So
317:   they have been banned from using it.
318: 
319: * iriver devices have problems with older versions of libmtp and
320:   with new devices libmtp does not know of as of yet, since it
321:   has an oldstyle USB device controller that cannot handle zero
322:   writes. (Register your device with us!) All their devices are
323:   likely to need a special device flag in the src/libusb-glue.c
324:   database.
325: 
326: * The Samsung Yepp T9 has several strange characteristics, some
327:   that we've managed to work around. (For example it will return
328:   multiple PTP packages in a single transaction.)
329: 
330: * The early firmware for Philips HDD players is known to be
331:   problematic. Please upgrade to as new firmware as you can get.
332:   (Yes this requires some kind of Windows Installation I think.)
333: 
334: * Philips HDD 1630/16 or 1630/17 etc may lock themselves up,
335:   turning inresponsive due to internal corruption. This typically
336:   gives an error in opening the PTP session. Apparently you can
337:   do a "repair" with the firmware utility (Windows only) which
338:   will often fix this problem and make the device responsive
339:   again.
340: 
341: * Some devices that implement GetObjectPropList (0x9805) will
342:   not return the entire object list if you request a list for object
343:   0xffffffffu. (But they should.) So they may need the special
344:   DEVICE_FLAG_BROKEN_MTPGETOBJPROPLIST_ALL.
345: 
346: * Some (smaller) subset of devices cannot even get all the
347:   properties for a single object in one go, these need the
348:   DEVICE_FLAG_BROKEN_MTPGETOBJPROPLIST. Currently only the
349:   iriver devices seem to have this bug.
350: 
351: * The Toshiba Gigabeat S (and probably its sibling the
352:   Microsoft Zune and other Toshiba devices) will only display
353:   album information tags for a song in case there is also
354:   an abstract album (created with the album interface) with
355:   the exact same name.
356: 
357: * The Zen Vision:M has an older firmware which is very corrupt,
358:   it is incompatible with the Linux USB stack altogether. The
359:   kernel dmesg will look something like this, and you have to
360:   upgrade the firmware using Windows:
361:   usb 4-5: new high speed USB device using ehci_hcd and address 5
362:   usb 4-5: configuration #1 chosen from 1 choice
363:   usb 4-5: can't set config #1, error -110
364: 
365: * The Sirus Stiletto does not seem to allow you to copy any files
366:   off the device. This may be someone's idea of copy protection.
367: 
368: * The Samsung P2 assigns parent folder ID 0 to all unknown file
369:   types.(i.e. moves them to the root folder)
370: 
371: * The Sandisk Sansa Clip+ needs a firmware upgrade in earlier
372:   versions in order to work properly.
373: 
374: 
375: New Devices
376: -----------
377: 
378: If you happen upon a device which libmtp claims it cannot
379: autodetect, please submit the vendor ID and device ID
380: (these can be obtained from the "lsusb" and "lsusb -n"
381: commands run as root) as a bug, patch or feature request
382: on the Sourceforge bug tracker at our homepage. If it
383: gives a sensible  output from "mtp-detect" then please attach
384: the result as well as it teach us some stuff about your
385: device. If you've done some additional hacking, join our
386: mailinglist and post your experiences there.
387: 
388: If you want to be able to hack some more and you're not
389: afraid of C hacking, add an entry for your device's
390: vendor/product ID and a descriptive string to the database
391: in the file src/music-players.h.
392: 
393: If you want to poke around to see if your device has some
394: special pecularities, you can test some special device
395: flags (defined in src/device-flags.h) by inserting them
396: together with your device entry in src/music-players.h.
397: Flags can be tested in isolation or catenated with "|"
398: (binary OR). If relatives to your device use a certain
399: flag, chances are high that a new device will need it
400: too, typically from the same manufacturer.
401: 
402: The most common flag that needs to be set is the
403: DEVICE_FLAG_UNLOAD_DRIVER that detach any Linux kernel
404: drivers that may have attached to the device making
405: MTP access impossible. This is however not expected to
406: really work: this is a problem being tracked as of
407: now (2007-08-04). See the "last resort" solutions below
408: if you really need to get your dual-mode device to work
409: with MTP.
410: 
411: Another flag which is easy to identify is the
412: DEVICE_FLAG_NO_ZERO_READS, which remedies connection
413: timeouts when getting files, and some timeouts on e.g.
414: successive "mtp-connect" calls.
415: 
416: If your device is very problematic we are curious of how it
417: works under Windows, so we enjoy reading USB packet sniffs
418: that reveal the low-level traffic carried out between
419: Windows Media Player and your device. This can be done
420: using e.g.:
421: 
422: * USBsnoop:
423:   https://benoit.papillault.free.fr/usbsnoop/
424: 
425: * The trial version of HHD Softwares software-only
426:   USB monitor. You need to get a copy of version 2.37 since
427:   the newer trial versions won't let you carry out the
428:   needed packet sniffs. (As of 2007-03-10 a copy can be found
429:   at: https://www.cobbleware.com/files/usb-monitor-237.exe)
430: 
431: There are other USB monitors as well, some more expensive
432: alternatives use hardware and even measure electronic
433: characteristics of the traffic (which is far too much
434: detail for us).
435: 
436: Device sniffs are an easy read since the PTP/MTP protocol
437: is nicely structured. All commands will have a structure such
438: as this in the log, we examplify with a object list request:
439: 
440: PTP REQEUST:
441: 000120: Bulk or Interrupt Transfer (UP), 03.09.2007 12:49:25.9843750 +0.0
442: Pipe Handle: 0x863ce234 (Endpoint Address: 0x2)
443: Send 0x20 bytes to the device:
444:  20 00 00 00 01 00 05 98 23 00 00 00 27 03 00 10    ......?#...'...
445:  Length      TYPE  CMD   Trans#      Param1
446: 
447:  00 00 00 00 02 DC 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00   .....Ü..........
448:  Param2      Param3      Param4      Param5
449: 
450: [OPTIONAL] DATA PHASE:
451: 000121: Bulk or Interrupt Transfer (UP), 03.09.2007 12:49:26.0 +0.0156250
452: Pipe Handle: 0x863ce214 (Endpoint Address: 0x81)
453: Get 0x1a bytes from the device:
454:  1A 00 00 00 02 00 05 98 23 00 00 00 01 00 00 00   .......?#.......
455:  Length      TYPE  CMD   Trans#      DATA
456: 
457:  27 03 00 10 02 DC 04 00 00 30                     '....Ü...0
458: 
459: RESPONSE:
460: 000122: Bulk or Interrupt Transfer (UP), 03.09.2007 12:49:26.0 +0.0
461: Pipe Handle: 0x863ce214 (Endpoint Address: 0x81)
462: Get 0xc bytes from the device:
463:  0C 00 00 00 03 00 01 20 23 00 00 00               ....... #...
464:  Length      TYPE  CODE  Trans#
465: 
466: * One send (OUT to the device), two reads (IN from the device).
467: 
468: * All three byte chunks commands are
469:   sent/recieved/recieeved by the function  ptp_transaction()
470:   in the file ptp.c.
471: 
472: * It boils down to ptp_usb_sendreq(), optionally ptp_usb_senddata()
473:   or ptp_usb_getdata() and finally ptp_usb_getresp() in the file
474:   libusb-glue.c. Notice ptp_usb_sendreq() and ptp_usb_getresp()
475:   are ALWAYS called. The TYPE field correspond to this, so the
476:   TYPES in this case are "COMMAND" (0x0001), "DATA" (0x0002),
477:   and "RESPONSE" (0x0003).
478: 
479: * Notice that the byte order is little endian, so you need to read
480:   each field from right to left.
481: 
482: * This COMMAND has:
483:   CMD 0x99805, we see in ptp.h that this is PTP_OC_MTP_GetObjPropList.
484:   Transaction# 0x00000023.
485:   REQUEST parameters 0x10000327, 0x00000000, 0x0000DC02, 0x00000000
486:     0x00000000, in this case it means "get props for object 0x10000327",
487:     "any format", "property 0xDC02" (PTP_OPC_ObjectFormat), then two
488:     parameters that are always zero (no idea what they mean or their
489:     use).
490: 
491: * The DATA has:
492:   CMD 0x99805, we see in ptp.h that this is PTP_OC_MTP_GetObjPropList.
493:   Transaction# 0x00000023.
494:   Then comes data 0x00000001, 0x10000327, 0xDC02, 0x0004, 0x3000
495:   Which means in this case, (and this is the tricky part) "here
496:   you have 1 property", "for object 0x10000327", "it is property
497:   0xDC02" (PTP_OPC_ObjectFormat), "which is of type 0x0004"
498:   (PTP_DTC_UINT16), "and set to 0x3000" (PTP_OFC_Undefined, it
499:   is perfectly valid to have undefined object formats, since it
500:   is a legal value defining this).
501: 
502: * This RESPONSE has:
503:   CMD 0x99805, we see in ptp.h that this is PTP_OC_MTP_GetObjPropList.
504:   Return Code ("RC") = 0x2001, PTP_RC_OK, all went fine.
505:   Transaction# 0x00000023.
506: 
507: If you want to compare the Windows behaviour with a similar
508: operation using libmtp you can go into the src/libusb-glue.c
509: file and uncomment the row that reads:
510: 
511: //#define ENABLE_USB_BULK_DEBUG
512: 
513: (I.e. remove the two //.)
514: 
515: This will make libmtp print out a hex dump of every bulk USB
516: transaction. The bulk transactions contain all the PTP/MTP layer
517: data, which is usually where the problems appear.

520: Notes to assist with debugging new devices:
521: -------------------------------------------
522: 
523: In debugging new hardware, we highly recommend that you only
524: use the example mtp-* applications that come with libmtp, as other
525: applications may have their own bugs that may interfere with your
526: new device working correctly. Using another application instead of
527: those that come with libmtp just adds another point of failure.
528: 
529: For debugging, there are 3 main options:
530: 
531: 1. Use the env variable: LIBMTP_DEBUG to increase the
532: verboseness of the debugging output for any application using
533: libmtp. Relevant codes are:
534: * 0x00 [0000 0000] : no debug (default)
535: * 0x01 [0000 0001] : PTP debug
536: * 0x02 [0000 0010] : Playlist debug
537: * 0x04 [0000 0100] : USB debug
538: * 0x08 [0000 1000] : USB data debug
539: // Codes are hex and binary respectively. Simple add them togther
540: // to get your desired level of output.
541: 
542: (Assuming bash)
543: eg:
544: $ export LIBMTP_DEBUG=12
545: $ mtp-detect
546:   // To get USB debug and USB data debug information.
547: 
548: $ export LIBMTP_DEBUG=2
549: $ mtp-detect
550:     // To get Playlist debug information.
551: 
552: Also note, an application may also use the LIBMTP_debug() API
553: function to achieve the same options as listed above.
554: 
555: 2. Use "strace" on the various mtp-* commands to see where/what
556: is falling over or getting stuck at.
557: * On Solaris and FreeBSD, use "truss" or "dtrace" instead on "strace".
558: * On Mac OS X, use "ktrace" or "dtrace" instead of "strace".
559: * On OpenBSD and NetBSD, use "ktrace" instead of "strace".
560: 
561: This will at least help pinpoint where the application is failing, or
562: a device is reporting incorrect information. (This is extremely helpful
563: with devices that have odd disconnection requirements).
564: 
565: The use of these tools may also pinpoint issues with libusb as
566: implemented by each OS vendor or issues with the MTP implementation
567: on the new device as well, so please be prepared for either case.
568: 
569: 3. Use "gdb" or similar debugger to step through the code as it is
570: run. This is time consuming, and not needed just to pinpoint where
571: the fault is.
572: 
573: The use of gdb or another debugger may also miss or actually cause
574: command and data timing issues with some devices, leading to false
575: information. So please consider this a last resort option.
576: 
577: Also please read the "It's Not Our Bug!" section below, as it does
578: contain some useful information that may assist with your device.
579: 
580: 
581: Dual-mode devices does not work - last resort:
582: ----------------------------------------------
583: 
584: Some devices that are dual-mode are simply impossible to get
585: to work under Linux because the usb-storage(.ko) kernel
586: module hook them first, and refuse to release them, even
587: when we specify the DEVICE_FLAG_UNLOAD_DRIVER flag. (Maybe
588: it DOES release it but the device will immediately be probed
589: at the USB mass storage interface AGAIN because it
590: enumerates.)
591: 
592: Here is what some people do:
593: 
594:  1. Plug in the device.
595:  2. USB-mass storage folder will open automatically.
596:  3. Unmount the device.
597:  4. Run mtp-detect. It will most likely fail the first time.
598:  5. Run mtp-detect again, it might work this time, or fail. Keep running
599:     till it works. 99% it works by the third try.
600:  6. Once mtp-detect gives you an "Ok", open either Rhythmbox or Gnomad2,
601:     everything should work.
602: 
603: Linux: Try this, if you have a recent Linux kernel,
604: add the file (as root):
605: 
606: /etc/modprobe.d/no-usb-storage.conf
607: 
608: With the contents:
609: 
610: options usb-storage quirks=1234:4321:i
611: 
612: This will tell usb-storage to ignore this device when it's inserted
613: so it is not hogged by the mass storage interfaces. Remove and re-insert
614: the device and see if it works. Usually this does the trick.
615: 
616: For older systems, or as a bigger hammer, run (as root) something
617: like:
618: 
619: > rmmod usb_storage ; mtp-detect
620: 
621: You can run most any command or a client like gnomad2 or
622: Amarok immediately after the rmmod command. This works
623: sometimes. Another even more brutal approach is this:
624: 
625: * Edit /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist
626: * Add the line "blacklist usb-storage"
627: * Reboot.
628: 
629: Now none of you USB disks, flash memory sticks etc will be
630: working (you just disabled them all). However you *can* try
631: your device, and it might have started working because there
632: is no longer a USB mass storage driver that tries to hook onto
633: the mass storage interface of your device.
634: 
635: If not even blacklisting works (check with
636: "lsmod | grep usb-storage"), there is some problem with
637: something else and you may need to remove or rename the file
638: /lib/modules/<VERSION>/kernel/drivers/usb/storage/usb-storage.ko
639: manually.
640: 
641: If you find the PerfectSolution(TM) to this dilemma, so you
642: can properly switch for individual devices whether to use it
643: as USB mass storage or not, please tell us how you did it. We
644: know we cannot use udev, because udev is called after-the-fact:
645: the device is already configured for USB mass storage when
646: udev is called.
647: 
648: On Mac OS there is another ugly hack:
649: 
650: 1. Open up a terminal window
651: 2. Type:
652: sudo mv /System/Library/Extensions/IOUSBMassStorageClass.kext
653: /System/Library/Extensions/IOUSBMassStorageClass.kext.disabled
654: 
655: and when prompted enter your password.
656: 
657: 3. Restart.
658: 
659: To reverse this change, just reverse the filenames:
660: 
661: sudo mv /System/Library/Extensions/
662: IOUSBMassStorageClass.kext.disabled /System/Library/Extensions/
663: IOUSBMassStorageClass.kext
664: 
665: and restart.

706: Lost symbols
707: ------------
708: 
709: Shared libraries can be troublesome to users not experienced with
710: them. The following is a condensed version of a generic question
711: that has appeared on the libmtp mailing list from time to time.
712: 
713: > PTP: Opening session
714: > Queried Creative Zen Vision:M
715: > gnomad2: relocation error: gnomad2: undefined symbol:
716: > LIBMTP_Get_Storageinfo
717: > (...)
718: > Are these type of errors related to libmtp or something else?
719: 
720: The problem is of a generic nature, and related to dynamic library
721: loading. It is colloquially known as "dependency hell".
722: (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependency_hell)
723: 
724: The gnomad2 application calls upon the dynamic linker in Linux to
725: resolve the symbol "LIBMTP_Get_Storageinfo" or any other symbol
726: (ELF symbol, or link point or whatever you want to call them, a
727: symbol is a label on a memory address that the linker shall
728: resolve from label to actual address.)
729: For generic information on this subject see the INSTALL file and
730: this Wikipedia page:
731: 
732: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_(computing)
733: 
734: When Linux /lib/ld-linux.so.X is called to link the symbols compiled
735: into gnomad2 (or any other executable using libmtp), it examines the
736: ELF file for the libmtp.so.X file it finds first and cannot resolve
737: the symbol "LIBMTP_Get_Storageinfo" (or whichever symbol you have a
738: problem witj) from it, since it's probably not there. There are many
739: possible causes of this symbol breakage:
740: 
741: 1) You installed precompiled libmtp and gnomad2 packages (RPMs, debs
742:     whatever) that do not match up. Typical cause: your gnomad2 package was
743:     built against a newer version of libmtp than what's installed on your
744:     machine. Another typical cause: you installed a package you found on
745:     the web, somewhere, the dependency resolution system did not protest
746:     properly (as it should) or you forced it to install anyway, ignoring
747:     some warnings.
748: 
749: 2) You compiled libmtp and/or gnomad2 from source, installing both or
750:     either in /usr/local/lib and /usr/local/bin. This means at compile-time
751:     gnomad2 finds the libmtp library in /usr/local/lib but at runtime, it
752:     depends on the Linux system wide library loader (/lib/ld-linux.so.X) in
753:     order to resolve the symbols. This loader will look into the file
754:     /etc/ld.so.conf and/or the folder /etc/ld.so.conf.d in order to find
755:     paths to libraries to be used for resolving the symbols. If you have
756:     some older version of libmtp in e.g. /usr/lib (typically installed by a
757:     package manager) it will take precedence over the new version you just
758:     installed in /usr/local/lib and the newly compiled library in
759:     /usr/local/lib will *not* be used, resulting in this error message.
760: 
761: 3) You really did install the very latest versions (as of writing libmtp
762:     0.1.5 and gnomad2 2.8.11) from source and there really is no
763:     pre-installed package of either on your machine. In that case I'm
764:     totally lost, I have no idea what's causing this.
765: 
766: Typical remedies:
767: 
768: 1) If you don't want to mess around with your system and risk these
769:     situations, only use pre-packaged software that came with the
770:     distribution or its official support channels. If it still breaks,
771:     blame your distribution, they're not packaging correctly. Relying on
772:     properly packaged software and not installing things yourself *is* the
773:     Linux solution to the "dependency hell" problem.
774: 
775: 2) Read about dynamically linked library handling until the stuff I wrote
776:     about in the previous list sounds like music to your ears, inspect
777:     your /lib, /usr/lib, /usr/local/lib, /etc/ld.so.conf and the
778:     /etc/ld.so.conf.d, remove all pre-packed versions using RPM, APT,
779:     YaST or whatever your distribution uses, compile libmtp and gnomad2
780:     (or whatever) from source only and you will be enlighted.
781: 
782: I don't know if this helps you, it's the best answer we can give.
783: 
784: 
785: API is obscure - I want plain files!
786: ------------------------------------
787: 
788: PTP/MTP devices does not actually contain "files", they contain
789: objects. These objects have file names, but that is actually
790: just a name tag on the object.
791: 
792: Folders/directories aren't really such entities: they are just
793: objects too, albeit objects that can act as parent to other
794: objects. They are called "associations" and are created in atomic
795: fashion and even though there is an MTP command to get all the
796: associations of a certain object, this command is optional
797: so it is perfectly possible (and most common, actually) to create
798: devices where the "folders" (which are actually associations) have
799: no idea whatsoever of what files they are associated as parents to
800: (i.e. which files they contain). This is very easy for device
801: manufacturers to implement, all the association (i.e. finding out
802: which files are in a certain folder) has to be done by the MTP
803: Initiator / host computer.
804: 
805: Moving a file to a new folder is for example very simple in a
806: "real" file system. In PTP/MTP devices it is often not even possible,
807: some devices *may* be able to do that, if they support command
808: 0x1019 "Move Object", but actually the only reliable way of executing
809: file movement is to upload the file to the host, download it with
810: the new parent, then delete the old file. We have played with the
811: idea of implementing this time consuming function as a fallback
812: in case the device does not support command 0x1019, perhaps one day
813: we will do that. (Some devices also support command 0x101a
814: "Copy Object".)
815: 
816: Then the issue that in PTP/MTP it is legal for two files to have
817: exactly the same path as long as their object IDs differ. A
818: folder/association can contain two files with the exact same name.
819: (And on the Creative devices this even works, too, though most devices
820: implicitly fail at this.) Perhaps one could add some custom hook for
821: handling that, so they become  /Foo.mp3 and /Foo.mp3(1) or something
822: similar, but it's really a bit kludgy.
823: 
824: Playlists and albums aren't really files, thinking about
825: them as files like the hacks in libgphoto2 is really backwards. They are
826: called associations and are more like a symbolic link that links in a
827: star-shaped pattern to all the files that are part of the album/playlist.
828: Some devices (Samsung) thought that was too complicated and have a
829: different way of storing playlists in an UTF-16 encoded .spl-like file
830: instead! This is why playlists/albums must have their own structs and
831: functions.
832: 
833: Plain file access also assumes to be able to write files of an
834: undetermined size, which is simply not possible in a transactional
835: file system like PTP/MTP. (See further below.)
836: 
837: 
838: I Want Streaming!
839: -----------------
840: 
841: Streaming reads is easy. Just connect the output file descriptor from
842: LIBMTP_Get_File_To_File_Descriptor() (and a similar function for tracks)
843: wherever you want.
844: 
845: People have connected this to TCP sockets for streaming web servers
846: etc, works like a charm. Some devices will even survive if the callback
847: functions return non-zero and cancel the download. Some devices will
848: lock up and even require a reset if you do that. Devices are poorly
849: implemented so that's life. If you want to stream off a device, the
850: best idea is always to stream the entire file and discard the stuff
851: at the end you don't want. It will incur a delay if you e.g. want to
852: skip between tracks, sadly.
853: 
854: Then we get to the complicated things: streaming WRITES...
855: 
856: There is a function:
857: LIBMTP_Send_File_From_File_Descriptor() (and similar for tracks)
858: which will write a file to a device from a file descriptor, which may
859: be a socket or whatever.
860: 
861: HOWEVER: this requires a piece of metadata with the .filesize properly
862: set first.
863: 
864: This is not because we think it is funny to require that, the protocol
865: requires it. The reason is that PTP/MTP is a transactional file system
866: and it wants to be able to deny file transfer if the file won't fit on
867: the device, so the transaction never even starts, it's impossible to
868: start a transaction without giving file length.
869: 
870: People really want streaming so I tried a lot of hacks to see if they
871: would work, such as setting file size to 0xffffffffU or something other
872: unnaturally big and then aborting the file transfer when the stream ends.
873: It doesn't work: either the device crashes or the file simply disappears
874: since the device rolls back all failed transactions.
875: 
876: So this is an inherent limitation of the PTP/MTP protocol.
877: 
878: 
879: I want to remote control my device!
880: -----------------------------------
881: 
882: I have both good and bad news for you.
883: 
884: The good news is that the MTP protocol has well-defined commands to play
885: back content on a device. Operation 0xD411 (PTP_DPC_MTP_PlaybackObject)
886: will start playing back a file on the device (whatever that may mean if
887: this is not a music or video file), and operation 0xD403 can set the
888: playback volume to save your ears. Then there are operations to
889: determine how far into the current file you currently are, so as to
890: support say progress bars.
891: 
892: Since these commands have been around since the dawn of the MTP protocol
893: and since it was developed in cooperation with Creative Technology, this
894: is probably a requested feature from the Creative people who already had
895: support for playback on their devices using the PDE protocol back then.
896: 
897: Anyway, here are the bad news:
898: [logs]$ grep d411 *
899: mtp-detect-trekstor-vibez.txt:   0xd411: Playback Object
900: 
901: Aha there is only one known device in the world which actually supports
902: playback on the device. So either you go buy the Trekstor Vibez, or you
903: can forget about this. You could always try asking your hardware vendor
904: of choice to go implement this.
905: 
906: Since none of the core developers of libmtp has the Trekstor device, this
907: is not yet implemented in libmtp.

913: If you are a device vendor there is a lot you can do for libmtp:
914: 
915: * Please consider assigning one of your employees as a contact person
916:   for libmtp, have them sign up to the libmtp development list and answer
917:   questions and post new device ID:s as they are released to our
918:   mailing list.
919: 
920: * If you want to help even more, assign someone to look deeper into
921:   error reports on your specific devices, understand why your firmware
922:   may require some special device flags and what can be done about it.
923: 
924: * Do you have spare devices you can give us? Send them to Richard (Mac
925:   support) or Linus (Linux support). (So far nobody did that except for
926:   Microsoft who sent us a Zune by proxy!)
927: 
928: Vendors do need help from libmtp too, especially we want to help
929: vendors improve their MTP stacks, because they all suffer from the
930: same problem: the lack of a proper conformance test has made many devices
931: incompliant with the MTP specification as it is published today: most
932: devices are just compliant with the Windows MTP stack, and don't work
933: out-of-the-box with libmtp. We need someone on the inside to help in
934: bug reporting vendors MTP stacks internally so these issues are raised.
935: A good way to go toward better MTP compliance is to test with an
936: alternative implementation of the stack. In e.g. IETF standardization
937: it is compulsory for an RFC to have atleast two independent implementations
938: for it to reach the status as standard.
939: 
940: Being compliant with libmtp is also more and more important for
941: vendors: libmtp is being deployed in some embedded systems like
942: set-top-boxes etc. It will be very irritating for customers if a device
943: will not dock properly with some home entertainment equipment just because
944: it is based on Linux and libmtp and not the Windows MTP stack.

946: Autodetect with gudev
947: ---------------------
948: 
949: Previously you would use HAL to detect devices being plugged in. Nowadays
950: we use udev directly, or though the GNOME libgudev library. LIBMTPs
951: default udev rules export the proper properties to detect any MTP device
952: automatically, here is a verbose example derived from gnomad2:
953: 
954: #define G_UDEV_API_IS_SUBJECT_TO_CHANGE
955: #include <gudev/gudev.h>
956: const char * const gudev_subsystems[] = { "usb", NULL };
957: GUdevClient *gudev_client;
958: guint uevent_id;
959: guint uevent_bus_hooked = 0;
960: guint uevent_device_hooked = 0;
961: 
962: 
963: static void uevent_cb(GUdevClient *client, const char *action, GUdevDevice *device, void *data)
964: {
965:   guint64 devicenum;
966:   guint vendor;
967:   guint model;
968:   guint busnum;
969:   guint devnum;
970:   guint mtpdevice;
971: 
972:   devicenum = (guint64) g_udev_device_get_device_number(device);
973:   g_print("%s event for %s (%"G_GINT64_MODIFIER"x)", action,
974:           g_udev_device_get_sysfs_path (device), devicenum);
975: 
976:   /* get device info */
977:   vendor = get_property_as_int(device, "ID_VENDOR_ID", 16);
978:   model = get_property_as_int(device, "ID_MODEL_ID", 16);
979:   busnum = get_property_as_int(device, "BUSNUM", 10);
980:   devnum = get_property_as_int(device, "DEVNUM", 10);
981:   mtpdevice = get_property_as_int(device, "ID_MTP_DEVICE", 10);
982: 
983:   if (vendor == 0 || model == 0) {
